title: Was This Neanderthal Murdered? - Nautilus
gist: A Scientific Reports study suggests Shanidar A, a roughly 45-year-old Neanderthal from about 75,000 years ago in Iraq's Shanidar Cave, had a circular puncture wound in his scapula, raising the possibility of a prehistoric murder.

insights.claim: The Shanidar Cave system in Iraq provided some of the first evidence that Neanderthals buried their dead.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.locator: The Shanidar Cave system in Iraq

insights.claim: A scapula from Shanidar A, a roughly 45-year-old Neanderthal man who lived around 75,000 years ago, has a circular hole a little wider than half an inch, interpreted as a puncture wound.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Raises the possibility of interpersonal violence among Neanderthals.

insights.claim: A new study in Scientific Reports raises the question of whether the wound indicates a prehistoric murder.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Framed as an open question, not a conclusion.
